# PiTTy v0.7.8

## Automatic Pi fork on upgrade

**Run `pitty upgrade` as usual.** PiTTy stages its private, memory-optimized Pi runtime together with the update. The next `pitty` launch activates it automatically. No separate fork installation or config migration is required.

- Includes tested patches for **Pi 1.5.2** and **pi-code-tool 0.6.2**. Large historical code-tool snapshots remain on disk until needed. New snapshots are compressed.
- The managed runtime does not modify the global `pi` executable, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, credentials, extension registrations, or session history. Your configured packages remain available. As before, `pitty upgrade` may separately refresh the installed profiled-subagent package.
- Existing `pi-code-tool` registrations retain their configuration, including `autoApprove`. PiTTy replaces the module inside its child process only, preventing duplicate-tool crashes.
- If the installed upstream Pi or code-tool version does not match the verified patch, PiTTy falls back to the existing global Pi. No partial patch is applied.
- Linux and macOS support the private runtime. Windows continues using the installed Pi.

### Performance measured on Linux

Against the same **2.47 GB** existing session, a complete PiTTy `-c` startup loaded history in **9.37 seconds**, with **571 MB peak Pi RSS**, and no crash. The earlier unmodified Pi process took roughly 25 seconds and could exhaust its 4 GB JavaScript heap. Results depend on session size and installed extensions.

### Controls and rollback

```bash
pitty upgrade                    # Stage the update and managed Pi fork
pitty                            # Activate on next launch
PITTY_USE_UPSTREAM_PI=1 pitty    # Use the original Pi
```

`PI_BIN=/path/to/pi` and `pitty --pi /path/to/pi` also override automatic selection. Existing running sessions are not restarted during the update.

**Source changes:** [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy/blob/v0.7.8/CHANGELOG.md). Fork memory patches: Pi `9ddb77c`, pi-code-tool `22a7a89`, included in the release with version and checksum guards.
